case_title: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Rakesh Mishra
accused_occupation: Gyanendra Singh Jadon: Building Officer, Municipal Corporation, Indore; Rakesh Mishra: Sub-Engineer, Municipal Corporation, Indore. Sajid Dhanani (not appealed against): Managing Director of Sayaji Hotel
statutory_provisions: Prevention of Corruption Act 1988 s.13(2) and s.13(1)(d); IPC s.120B (criminal conspiracy)
evidence_type: Documentary (charge-sheet and accompanying material); no trial evidence assessed at this pre-trial stage
trial_court_outcome: Ordered framing of charges under PC Act s.13(2), s.13(1)(d) r/w IPC s.120B against three accused; no sentence (pre-trial)
high_court_outcome: Revision petitions allowed; order framing charges set aside
neutral_facts: The proprietor of a multi-storied hotel and adjoining club in Indore obtained a building permission in 1993, valid for one year, with renewal required before a set date. A revised building plan was later submitted to the Building Officer, who approved it along with a renewal of the permission, and a completion certificate for the adjoining club was granted shortly afterwards. The prosecution alleged that the revised plan was a complete departure from the original plan, with the built-up area of the hotel increased substantially and that of the club's ground floor decreased markedly. It was alleged that the revision was sanctioned without approval from the high-rise building committee and without electricity, water supply, sewage and fire-safety clearances. It was further alleged that the completion certificate was issued only seven days after the revision of the permission, although the club could not plausibly have been completed with all compliances within that time. A Sub-Engineer in the building permission branch was alleged to have made notings in the note sheet favouring the proprietor. It was alleged that the Building Officer received free lifetime honorary membership of the club for himself and five family members as illegal gratification. The Building Officer was also alleged to have failed to inform the property tax department about the completion certificate, leading to alleged tax evasion of Rs.5,49,000. An anti-corruption agency registered a first information report in January 1998 and, after investigation, filed a charge-sheet against the three accused.
number_of_offences: 3 charged; 0 finally upheld (charges restored for trial; no conviction)
financial_property_loss: Alleged property tax evasion of Rs.5,49,000 (alleged only; the High Court noted the amount was later paid)
premeditation_planning: Not stated (the court did not decide; conspiracy was alleged)
motive: alleged: illegal gratification in the form of free lifetime honorary membership of the Sayaji Club
key_evidence_accepted: Prima facie material: the revised plan was a complete departure from the original (built-up areas changed sharply); completion certificate issued 7 days after revision; revision granted without committee approval; acceptance of honorary club membership
trial_duration: offence: not given (FIR lodged 18-01-1998); trial judgment: not given (order framing charges, date not stated); High Court: 18.05.2007; Supreme Court: 23.03.2015
legal_representation: State (appellant): Arvind Varma, Deepika Shari, C. D. Singh; Accused (respondents): Sumit Kumar Sharma, Niraj Sharma, Brajesh Kumar
investigation_status: FIR lodged 18-01-1998 by anti-corruption agency; investigation completed; charge-sheet filed; charges framed; trial not yet concluded
procedural_irregularity: Court noted disappointment at extended pre-trial litigation and delay; no specific procedural lapse found
appeal_history: Trial court: charges framed against three accused. High Court: revision petitions allowed, framing of charges set aside. Supreme Court: State's appeals allowed, High Court order set aside, framing of charges restored
prosecution_argument: The High Court exceeded permissible limits by examining the merits at the pre-trial stage; various authorities were cited in support
defence_argument: Building Officer was in office only from 31.10.1994 to 16.10.1996 and cannot be liable for acts before or after; permission predated his appointment; High Court's revision jurisdiction includes inherent power under s.482 Cr.P.C.; no legal duty to inform property tax department
legal_principle_applied: At framing of charges, only the charge-sheet and accompanying material are considered; the test is prima facie case and the subjective satisfaction of the framing court
precedent_relied_upon: Not stated (authorities referred to but not named in the judgment)
other_sentence_order: Request to the Trial Court to conduct the trial in the most expeditious manner

case_title.quote: STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH A v. RAKESH MISHRA

number_of_accused.quote: the State has assailed the impugned judgment only against Rakesh Mishra and GS. Jadon.

accused_gender.quote: As against Rakesh Mishra, the charge was of criminal conspiracy, for the reason that he was the Sub-Engineer at the relevant time

accused_occupation.quote: Gyanendra Singh Jadon was working at the relevant time as Building Officer posted at Municipal Corporation, Indore and Rakesh Mishra was working as Sub-Engineer, Municipal Corporation, Indore.

offence_category.quote: the offences under Section 13(2) and Section 13(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act and Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code

statutory_provisions.quote: Sections 13(2) and 13(1) (d) of Prevention of Corruption Act read with Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1960.

evidence_type.quote: only charge-sheet along with the accompanying material is to be considered at the stage of framing of charges

trial_court_outcome.quote: The First Additional Sessions Judge/ Special Judge, Indore, after perusing the charge-sheet and accompanying documents ordered framing of charges against the three accused

high_court_outcome.quote: By the impugned judgment the High Court of Madhya Pradesh has allowed the three revision petitions, setting aside the orders of the First Additional Judge/ Special Judge, Indore, for framing charges

final_outcome.quote: Therefore, these criminal appeals are allowed, the order passed by the High Court is set aside and the order of the Addi. Sessions Judge framing charges is restored.

neutral_facts.quote: It is alleged that these three accused hatched a criminal conspiracy in which G.S. Jadon and Rakesh Mishra illegally granted a Building Certificate and a Completion Certificate to Sayaji Hotel in Indore.

attempt_completion.quote: It is alleged that these three accused hatched a criminal conspiracy in which G.S. Jadon and Rakesh Mishra illegally granted a Building Certificate and a Completion Certificate

number_of_offences.quote: Sections 13(2) and 13(1)(d) of Prevention of Corruption Act read with Section 120B of the Indian Penal Code, 1960.

financial_property_loss.quote: It is also alleged that he did not inform about the completion certificate to the Property Tax Department of Indore Municipal Corporation leading to evasion of tax by the Hotel amounting to Rs.5,49,000/-.

premeditation_planning.quote: It is alleged that these three accused hatched a criminal conspiracy

motive.quote: Allegedly, as illegal gratification, Sayaji Hotel provided free lifetime honorary membership to G.S. Jadon and his family members in the Sayaji Club.

key_evidence_accepted.quote: the revised building plan, which was sanctioned in guise of the revision of sanction of the building permission, was a complete departure from the original plan.

trial_duration.quote: Criminal Revision No. 636 of 2007. From the Judgment and Order dated 18.05.2007 of the High Court of Madhya Pradesh at Indore

legal_representation.quote: Arvind Varma, Deepika Shari, C. D. Singh for the Appellant. Sumit kumar Sharma, Niraj Sharma, Brajesh Kumar for the Respondent.

investigation_status.quote: After investigation the police filed charge-sheet against the three accused persons.

procedural_irregularity.quote: We may, however, express our disappointment of such extended litigation at the pre-trial stage itself.

appeal_history.quote: The High Court allowed the Revision Petitions and set aside the order of framing charges passed by the Addi. Sessions Judge, Indore.

prosecution_argument.quote: The major argument advanced by the State of Madhya Pradesh before us has been that the High Court traversed beyond the permissible limit while deciding the legality of order framing charges, being a pre-trial stage.

defence_argument.quote: He cannot be held liable for any act/omission done prior to or after this period. It is contended that building permission was granted to Sayaji Hotel prior to his appointment as the Building Officer.

legal_principle_applied.quote: only charge-sheet along with the accompanying material is to be considered at the stage of framing of charges, so as to satisfy whether a prima facie case is made out.

precedent_relied_upon.quote: Various authorities have been cited before us to prove that point.
